data.title: Motilal Oswal launches ₹3,000 cr fund to invest in Grade A office spaces
data.description:
Motilal Oswal Alternates, the alternative investments arm of the Motilal Oswal Group, has launched a new fund targeting a corpus of up to ₹3,000 crore to invest in India's Grade A commercial office developments, seeking to tap growing institutional demand for quality office space.
 
The India Assets Excellence Fund – I (IAEF I) will have a base target corpus of ₹1,500 crore, with a green shoe option to raise an additional ₹1,500 crore. The fund will invest in early-stage office developments through equity joint ventures with established developers across Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Mumbai, the National Capital Region (NCR), Pune and Chennai.
 
The fund has a tenure of eight years and is registered with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) as a Category II Alternative Investment Fund (AIF). The sponsor and employees will together commit ₹200 crore, aligning their interests with those of investors.
 
 
MO Alternates expects the fund to achieve its first close by December 2026 and complete fundraising within 12 months of its launch.
 
Why is the fund targeting early-stage office developments?
 
The fund's launch comes amid a strengthening commercial real estate market, with demand for Grade A office space supported by Global Capability Centres (GCCs), flexible workspace operators, banking, financial services and insurance (BFSI) companies and technology firms.
 
According to the company, Grade A office stock across India's leading cities is projected to reach approximately one billion square feet in the coming quarters. Net absorption has exceeded new supply for several quarters, including in 2026, while overall vacancy has declined to around 15%. Vacancy in core micro-markets has fallen to low single-digit levels.
 
Despite these favourable demand indicators, institutional capital in Indian commercial real estate has largely focused on completed, income-generating properties.
 
IAEF I intends to address this funding gap by entering projects at an earlier stage, when land acquisition, approvals and construction are underway, and participating in the value created as developments progress towards leasing and stabilisation.
 
The fund will invest through equity joint ventures with established developers rather than directly purchasing completed office buildings. Its investment strategy is to participate across the development cycle and eventually exit through institutional monetisation of stabilised assets.
 
 How will the fund generate returns?
 
Unlike investments in completed commercial properties, where investors typically earn rental income and benefit from potential capital appreciation, early-stage development investments carry exposure to the entire project lifecycle.
 
The fund will provide equity alongside developers and seek to benefit from the increase in asset value as projects move from development to construction, tenant acquisition and stabilised occupancy.
 
The strategy also draws on the expanding institutional market for completed office assets, including Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs) and core-plus funds, which can provide potential exit routes for stabilised properties.
 
However, early-stage development investments carry additional risks, including construction delays, cost overruns, slower-than-expected leasing, changes in occupier demand and difficulties in securing exits at the expected valuations.
 
The eight-year fund tenure means investors should also be prepared for a relatively long investment horizon and limited liquidity compared with listed real estate investment vehicles.
 
 What is the fund manager's track record?
 
MO Alternates manages cumulative assets under management (AUM) of more than ₹30,000 crore across real estate, private equity and private credit.
 
Its real estate platform has operated six India Realty Excellence Fund (IREF) vintages since 2009, making more than 200 investments and securing over 150 exits.
 
The company reports a gross internal rate of return (IRR) of approximately 20% on exited investments across these vintages. It has also funded more than ₹11,000 crore across residential and commercial projects, working with over 60 developer partners.
 
The reported 20% gross IRR relates to exited investments across its previous funds and should not be interpreted as a projected or assured return for investors in the new fund. Actual investor returns will depend on the performance of IAEF I's investments, expenses, fees and the timing and value of exits.
 
 Domestic capital eyes India's office real estate opportunity
 
The launch also reflects an attempt to increase domestic institutional participation in a commercial property segment where global capital has historically played a significant role.
 
For investors, the fund offers exposure to commercial real estate development through an alternative investment structure, rather than through direct ownership of office properties or listed REITs.
 
However, the strategy is not without risk. Investors will need to evaluate the fund's investment selection, developer partnerships, project-level debt, fee structure, expected holding period and exit assumptions before committing capital.
 
The fund's performance will ultimately depend on its ability to deliver projects on time, secure quality tenants and monetise completed assets at attractive valuations. 
"Demand from Global Capability Centres, flexible workspaces and leading domestic enterprises continues to outpace new supply, absorption has run ahead of completions for several quarters, and Grade A vacancy is compressing. REITs have given the asset class an institutional depth it lacked a decade ago, and together with core-plus funds have created a proven exit market for stabilized assets. Yet institutional capital at early stage remains scarce, even though that is where the largest share of value is created. MO Alternates has been at the forefront of identifying such opportunities for its investors, and that gap is what IAEF I has been built to address," said Saurabh Rathi, Managing Director & Co-Head, Real Estate Funds, MO Alternates.
 
"This is an opportune moment for a dedicated commercial real estate fund, and IAEF I has been designed to seize it. The sector is one of the most compelling investment themes in Indian real assets today, and one that global capital has so far dominated. With this fund, we are opening Grade A office development to domestic capital, and intend to play a pivotal role in that shift. We will enter early through structured equity, alongside established developers across India’s Tier-1 markets, and participate in the value created as projects move from land and approvals through construction to leased, stabilized assets with clear routes to institutional monetization. Our aim is to give investors exposure across the full development cycle, with the discipline that has defined our real estate platform," said Anand Lakhotia, Managing Director & Co-Head, Real Estate Funds, MO Alternates. 
MO Alternates expects to achieve the first close of IAEF I by year-end and to complete fundraising within 12 months of launch.

data.title: Gold Spot comeback: How the orange drink became a hit, then disappeared
data.description:
Coca-Cola is reportedly preparing to bring back Gold Spot, its orange-flavoured fizzy drink, after a 26-year hiatus. According to a report in The Economic Times, Gold Spot, which was acquired by Coca-Cola from the Parle group in 1993, is expected to return in a low-sugar or no-sugar formulation as the beverage maker looks to tap changing consumer preferences and counter intensifying competition.
 
The reported revival also found an unlikely social media moment over the weekend when photographs of former Indian cricket team captain MS Dhoni and his wife, Sakshi, with Gold Spot cans went viral on social media. However, it remains unclear whether Dhoni has been signed to endorse the brand.
 
 
Gold Spot, known for its taglines 'Zing Thing' and 'Livva Little Hot, Sippa Gold Spot', was discontinued by Coca-Cola in 2000 to make way for its global orange drink Fanta.
 
From Parle's stable to Coca-Cola
 
Gold Spot was launched by Parle in 1952, when India's packaged soft drink market was still taking shape. Its orange flavour and distinctive positioning made it one of the country's familiar home-grown fizzy drinks. Its advertising tagline, 'Zing Thing', was an instant hit among the youth.
 
Parle's beverage portfolio grew over the years to include Limca, launched in 1971, Maaza in 1974 and Thums Up in 1978. These brands gained ground after Coca-Cola exited India in 1977, following disagreements with the government over foreign ownership rules and requirements to disclose proprietary information.
 
Parle sold Gold Spot to Coca-Cola when the latter returned to India in 1993. Coca-Cola also acquired Parle's other beverage brands, including Thums Up, Limca, Maaza, Rim Zim and Citra. The deal also gave Coca-Cola a ready-made portfolio of Indian drinks with considerable consumer recognition. 
ALSO READ: L&T bags large order worth ₹5,000 crore to deploy AI cluster in Chennai
 
Why Gold Spot disappeared
 
Gold Spot and Fanta occupied the same broad orange-flavoured carbonated drinks category. Coca-Cola eventually chose to concentrate its efforts behind Fanta, its established international brand, and phased out Gold Spot in 2000. A 2009 Business Today report noted that the company had struggled to manage overlapping brands after acquiring Parle's portfolio.
 
Other drinks such as Thums Up and Limca continued under Coca-Cola and retained distinct positions in the Indian market.
 
Why bring it back now?
 
The reported revival comes as India's carbonated drinks market becomes more competitive, with Reliance Consumer Products' Campa and regional challenger Lahori Zeera are gaining ground in a market traditionally dominated by Coca-Cola and PepsiCo.
 
According to a report in The Economic Times, the combined market share of smaller players, led by Campa and Lahori Zeera, nearly doubled to 15 per cent in January-September 2025, from around 7 per cent a year earlier. The combined share of Coca-Cola and PepsiCo fell to about 85 per cent from 93 per cent over the same period.
 
In April, Reliance said its beverages brand Campa has become the fourth-largest carbonated soft drinks player in India, with over ₹4,700 crore in gross sales in FY26 and a double-digit market share in key markets. ITC has also entered the segment with its sugar-free Coconut Cola, priced at ₹60 for a 250-ml can, targeting consumers willing to pay a premium for alternative formulations.
 
The other significant shift is towards beverages with lower sugar content. Sales of zero- and low-sugar drinks in India rose significantly, moving from about 5 per cent of the overall beverage market in 2020 to an average of roughly 30 per cent by 2025, and surging even higher through 2026, according to media reports.
 
Gold Spot, which Coca-Cola is reportedly bringing back in a low-sugar or no-sugar formulation, could therefore tap into a growing market for drinks that offer the taste of traditional soft drinks with less sugar.

data.title: Superintelligence is arriving: Meta AI chief urges rethink of AI future
data.description:
Meta Chief AI Officer Alexandr Wang has warned that artificial intelligence (AI) is approaching 'superintelligence' and urged the industry to rethink the technology’s future.
 
In a blog post on X, Wang said, “How humanity acts over the next year will have great consequence on what future world we live in."
 
He argued that advances in AI suggest intelligence itself may no longer be the main obstacle to surpassing human performance across fields.
 
Comparing the progress to the mathematical milestone of proving the Riemann Hypothesis, Wang said such an achievement would mark a significant turning point in AI development. He described it as potentially the greatest intellectual accomplishment in human history, arguing that completing it with the help of an AI system would demonstrate capabilities that humans do not fully understand.
 
 
The Riemann Hypothesis is a 167-year-old mathematical conjecture concerning the distribution of prime numbers and remains one of mathematics’ most significant unsolved problems. On November 21, a mathematician at Anthropic claimed to have found a proof of the hypothesis with the help of Claude, although the breakthrough is still undergoing mathematical scrutiny.
 

How AI models moved from maths to general-purpose tasks

 
Wang pointed to AI models’ performance in the American Invitational Mathematics Examination (AIME) in December 2024 as an early indication of the scale of progress in AI. He recalled that models beginning to solve the examination’s hardest problems prompted a realisation that AI capabilities were advancing rapidly.
 
“For those who did math competitions, there was a similar moment of ‘oh shit everything is about to change’ when the models began acing the AIME in December 2024 with o3,” he wrote.
 
Wang said the significance of this development was that the hardest AIME problems required a level of intellectual ability far beyond what most engineers, business professionals and other workers encounter in their everyday tasks.
 
He argued that while AI models initially faced limitations in domain-specific knowledge, context and practical execution, a lack of raw intelligence was not the fundamental bottleneck. Progress over the subsequent two years in addressing these limitations had enabled advances in coding, cybersecurity and agentic capabilities, turning AI models into increasingly capable general-purpose assistants.
 
“The Riemann Hypothesis may be the most intellectually demanding problem humanity has ever devised, which some of the most brilliant humans over the past 150 years have dedicated their lives to,” he said.
 
Wang said the remaining challenges were now less about intelligence and more about domain-specific expertise, infrastructure and experimentation.
 
“The remaining gaps for models to greatly surpass humanity in every field are no longer intelligence; they are domain-specific know-how, plumbing, and experimentation. This means it is likely that AI will become the greatest contributor of progress across nearly every field, vastly outperforming the best humans,” he said.
 

Could AI surpass humans across research fields?

 
The implications of AI extend well beyond mathematics and software development, Wang argued, adding that it could become the biggest driver of progress across nearly every field of study.
 
“Most researchers would agree that AI research is certainly much less intellectually demanding than solving the Riemann Hypothesis. The models are clearly going to be intelligent enough to automate all of AI research and be clearly superhuman at improving themselves—along with massively accelerating biological research, weapons research, economics research, and more,” he wrote.
 

Why Wang wants a rethink of AI safety and human control

 
Wang said the industry needed to think carefully about the future it wanted to create and how to achieve it. He questioned whether humanity would be able to retain control over AI systems capable of unrestricted recursive self-improvement, or over superintelligence that is 1,000 times more capable than humans across every field.
 
“I notice a particular form of lazy thinking within the AI industry, which is that ASI (artificial superintelligence) is inevitable and the only problem to solve is how to do it safely, but there is much more at stake,” he wrote.
 
Wang argued that humanity should not accept a future in which control over society is effectively handed over to AI systems. Instead, the industry should focus on building technology that gives people greater agency and empowerment.
 
“We should not be okay with a ‘handover’ of society to AI. We should endeavour ourselves to build a technology which delivers a positive future for humanity, where all humans have greater agency and empowerment,” Wang said.
 
He added that achieving such a future would require the entire AI industry to take a different course from the default path of development, while maintaining that a positive outcome for humanity remained possible.

data.title: Low P/E investing alone is a bad strategy: Harini Dedhia explains why
data.description:
Disclaimer: This article is written by Harini Dedhia, fund manager at Tamohara Investment Managers. Views expressed are her own. Readers' discretion is advised.
 Two recent moves in the market have everyone convinced of the ‘purist’ view of value investing. The first saw NIFTY IT move 17.5 per cent in the month of October alone; starting from a bottom valuation of 17.7 P/E (Price-to-Earnings Ratio) vs. the 10 year median of 25.1. The second saw NIFTY 50 move 16 per cent from the bottom it made on 8th October; from a 19 P/E vs. the 10 year median for the index at 23.2.
 
 
This has convinced many investors that buying companies within a certain P/E band alone is a good strategy. That has, however, not been the case in India, at least for the past 10 years. Almost the opposite has always been true. “Expensive” stocks are so because of the strength in underlying earnings growth and that momentum in earnings has sustained, securing returns for investors. 
 
Looking at the ten most expensive and cheap companies in NIFTY50 by trailing twelve months P/E Ratio reveals that the opposite has been true. Expensive companies on average (and median) have outperformed the benchmark by a margin.
 
For the past 10Y, NIFTY 50 has delivered a CAGR of 12.5 per cent. Only 2 of 10 companies from the ‘Cheap Ten’ have beaten that 10Y performance. For ‘Expensive Ten’ the number is 8 out 10.  
 
Favorable valuation ex of growth has no bearing on stock price performance. Both the companies from ‘Cheap Ten’ that have outperformed the index are ones that have outperformed on earnings too. Both Hindalco and SBI have respectively demonstrated a 10Y EPS CAGR of 76 per cent and 19 per cent. The 10Y average EPS growth is also solely skewed by this earnings performance by Hindalco. Ex of this, the average is much closer to the median EPS CAGR at 11 per cent.  
ALSO READ: Stock Market LIVE: Sensex down 800 pts, Nifty below 25,600; Nifty Defence drops 1%
 
There is only one company in the ‘Cheap Ten’ bucket that has delivered 10Y EPS growth of over NIFTY 50’s EPS growth at 14.5 per cent (100bps over benchmark’s) but has still underperformed NIFTY50’s CAGR at 11.25 per cent (125bps under the benchmark CAGR). No points for guessing that this company is HDFC Bank and perhaps the hunting ground for structural investment ideas. 
 
It is not surprising that this relationship between earnings growth and stock price is seen in the underperformers from the ‘Expensive 10’ group as well. The two companies that have underperformed the index have done so on earnings growth as well- Asian Paints by 360bps at 9.9 per cent EPS CAGR and Hindustan Unilever by 60bps at 12.9 per cent EPS CAGR.  
One can attempt to discredit this assessment by stating that the current trailing twelve month P/E captures the up move these companies have seen and therefore is not the appropriate tool. Even if we recreate the ‘Expensive 10’ and ‘Cheap 10’ based on the historical 10Y average P/E, the answer does not change. The difference in performance remains stark.  
 
The same two companies are the underperformers from the ‘Expensive 10’ category on a 10Y basis. Perhaps the trap to avoid is higher P/E stocks with decelerating growth rather than higher P/E stocks altogether.

data.title: Vishal Mega Mart gains 3%; here's why analysts are bullish on stock
data.description:
Vishal Mega Mart share price today Share price of Vishal Mega Mart rose 3.3 per cent to an intraday high of ₹95 in Monday's trading session despite a sharp fall in the benchmark indices. Analysts reckon that the stock offers a favourable risk-reward ratio on hopes of healthy demand traction in Q2FY27. Vishal Mega Mart has rallied over 12 per cent thus far in November. However, in the preceding two months the stock crashed nearly 24 per cent, and trades with a loss of over 38 per cent thus far in 2026. The stock hit a 52-week high of ₹139.50 on December 19, 2025, and a 52-week low of ₹84.16 on November 02, 2026. At 11:23 AM on Monday, Vishal Mega Mart traded 2.6 per cent higher at ₹94.45 amid trades of around 59 lakh shares on the NSE. Meanwhile, the Nifty 50 index was down 0.8 per cent at 25,600 levels. ICICI Securities maintains 'Buy' rating on stock Analysts at ICICI Securities in a report dated November 22, 2026, maintained a 'Buy'  rating on Vishal Mega Mart, with a target price of ₹150. The target price implies a potential upside of nearly 59 per cent from current levels. The brokerage reckons that Vishal Mega Mart offers an attractive near-term buying opportunity, supported by expected healthy demand traction in Q3FY27, potential support for profitability, and attractive valuations. 
ALSO READ: Stock Market LIVE: Sensex slumps 900 pts, Nifty below 25,600; Nifty Defence drops 1%
 
 In Q2FY27, the company's revenue grew by 14 per cent year-on-year, while reported Same Stores Sales Growth (SSSG) was ~5.4 per cent. Adjusting for the festive shift, Q2 SSSG was ~9 per cent, said analysts. Further, the Vishal's management indicated no demand moderation in October 2026, noting strong demand momentum leading into Diwali and the wedding season. "Importantly, with festivals such as Durga Puja and Dussehra shifting into Q3, which are clothing-centric, the quarter could see a higher bias toward apparel sales (margin-accretive), aiding gross margins. To achieve its full-year double-digit target, management expects Q3 SSSG to exceed 10 per cent," the brokerage said in its report. ICICI Securities notes that Vishal Mega Mart's private-label portfolio, loyalty strength and expanding omnichannel presence,  alongside improving demand prospects, support the near-term momentum. However, despite these fundamentals, the stock has underperformed (down ~25 per cent in six months). "Given the current attractive valuations, and growth catalysts in Q3 led by deferred festive spending, the stock appears a good buy for the near term. The stock is currently trading at a P/E of ~33x on FY28E EPS," the brokerage firm said. Disclaimer: Views and outlook in this report belong to the brokerages and analysts cited. They do not reflect the views of Business Standard. Readers are advised to exercise discretion.

data.title: Ireland extends visa waiver for Indians until December 2026: How to qualify
data.description:
Want to visit Ireland this winter? Travellers from India can do so without applying for a separate Irish visa if they meet the eligibility conditions under the country's Short-Stay Visa Waiver Programme, which has been extended until December 31, 2026.
 
The extension was announced on the official portal of Ireland's Department of Justice, Home Affairs and Migration. The programme, which was originally due to expire on October 31, 2026, has been extended by two months, keeping the facility available through the Christmas and New Year holiday season.
 
Under the scheme, eligible travellers holding a qualifying UK short-stay visitor or business visa can also visit the Republic of Ireland without submitting a separate Irish visa application. An Irish short-stay visa normally costs €60 for a single entry and €100 for multiple entries, excluding visa application centre service charges.
  
First introduced in July 2011 to encourage tourism and business travel from emerging markets, the programme has been extended several times. The latest extension offers some relief to Indian travellers planning winter holidays. This is particularly relevant because Ireland removed the right to appeal short-stay visa refusals from June 1, 2026, requiring rejected applicants to submit fresh applications instead.
 

How does Ireland's visa waiver programme work?

 
Holding a valid UK visa alone does not make a traveller eligible for the waiver. Applicants must meet specific entry and stay conditions, according to Ireland's Immigration Service Delivery.
 
Enter the UK first: Travellers must first enter the United Kingdom using their qualifying UK visa and clear immigration control before proceeding to Ireland. Those flying directly from India or another third country to Dublin cannot use the waiver. An exception applies to travellers who have already used a multiple-entry UK visa to enter the UK on an earlier trip and still have valid permission to stay.
 
Stay for up to 90 days: Visitors can remain in Ireland for a maximum of 90 days or until their UK permission to stay expires, whichever comes first.
 
The arrangement is not reciprocal: The waiver allows eligible UK visa holders to visit Ireland, but an Irish short-stay visa does not permit entry into the UK, including Northern Ireland. Travellers entering Northern Ireland and then crossing into the Republic of Ireland will need a double-entry or multiple-entry UK visa if they intend to return to Northern Ireland.
 
Border checks still apply: Irish immigration officers retain the authority to question travellers and refuse entry. Visitors should carry their passport containing the used UK visa, evidence of their entry into the UK, return tickets, accommodation bookings and proof of sufficient funds.
 

Which countries are eligible for Ireland's visa waiver?

 
The programme covers nationals of 21 countries, including India. The complete list is:
 
India, China (excluding Hong Kong and Macau), Indonesia, Kazakhstan, the Philippines, Thailand, Uzbekistan, Vietnam, Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia, Turkey, Colombia and Peru.
 
However, not every category of UK visa qualifies for the facility.
 
Eligible UK visas:
 
Standard short-stay visitor visas.
Short-stay business visas granted for stays of up to 180 days.
 
UK permissions not covered:
 
Electronic Travel Authorisations (ETAs).
Transit visas.
Marriage and civil partnership visitor visas.
Long-term visas, including student, work and family reunification permissions exceeding 180 days.
 
There is also an important distinction for nationals of the 21 eligible countries who live in the UK on long-term visas. They cannot use the waiver and must apply separately for an Irish visa. However, they are exempt from the Irish visa application fee.
 

How does Ireland's visa appeal rule affect Indian travellers?

 
The visa waiver extension comes at a time when Indian travellers face tighter procedures for challenging Irish visa refusals.
 
From June 1, 2026, Ireland removed the right to appeal refusals of short-stay (Type C) visas. The change applies to applicants of all nationalities, including Indians applying for tourist, business or family-visit visas. Limited exceptions apply to cases covered by the EU Free Movement Directive.
 
Under the revised rules, applicants whose short-stay visa applications are rejected on or after June 1 cannot challenge the decision through the earlier appeal process. They must submit fresh applications, addressing the reasons for the previous rejection.
 
The change applies to short-stay visas and does not mean that Indian travellers are barred from applying for an Irish visa. It also does not affect their eligibility for the Short-Stay Visa Waiver Programme, provided they meet its conditions.
 

Will Ireland extend the visa waiver programme beyond 2026?

 
Irish immigration authorities have not yet confirmed whether the programme will continue beyond December 31, 2026.
 
Travellers planning trips that extend beyond this date should check the Immigration Service Delivery portal for further announcements or apply for a separate Irish visa well in advance.
 
Separately, Indian and Chinese nationals are also covered by the British-Irish Visa Scheme (BIVS), a distinct arrangement that allows eligible travellers to visit both the UK and Ireland using a single visa endorsed under the scheme.

data.title: BSE Realty index soars 17% in November; what's driving real estate stocks?
data.description:
BSE Realty index movement

 
Shares of real estate companies extended their rally, with the BSE Realty index hitting a 52-week high of 7,401.10, gaining 1 per cent on the BSE in Monday’s intraday deals on expectations of an improved demand outlook in the second half of the financial year 2026-27 (H1FY27). The realty index quoted at its highest level since November 6, 2025.
 
At 11:37 AM, the BSE Realty index was up 0.48 per cent at 7,355.19, while the Nifty Realty index was up 0.30 per cent. In comparison, the BSE Sensex and Nifty 50 indices were down 0.80 per cent each. The Nifty Realty index also hit a 52-week high of 947.70 on the National Stock Exchange (NSE) in intraday trade. 
 
 
Thus far in the month of November 2026, the BSE Realty index outperformed the market by soaring 16.6 per cent, compared to a 11.85 per cent rise in the BSE Sensex. Aditya Birla Real Estate, Lodha Developers, Prestige Estates Projects, Godrej Properties and Phoenix Mills rallied between 18-23 per cent in November.
 
Since April, the realty index zoomed 47 per cent. Share price of Sri Lotus Developers and Realty more than doubled or skyrocketed 129 per cent, while Lodha Developers and DLF surged 82 per cent and 58 per cent, respectively. Phoenix Mills, Godrej Properties, Prestige Estates Projects and Oberoi Realty soared in the range of 32-54 per cent during the period.
 

What’s driving real estate stocks?

 
Motilal Oswal Financial Services (MOFSL) said that its real estate coverage universe reported 26 per cent year-on-year (YoY) pre-sales growth in the July to September 2026 quarter (Q2FY27), led by a 7x jump for Oberoi Realty with its stellar foray in NCR. Excluding Oberoi Realty, MOFSL’s coverage posted 3 per cent YoY growth, which was on expected lines, despite no major launches. 
 
“For our coverage, 2QFY27 pre-sales at ₹42,800 crore were the third highest quarterly performance in any year despite Q2 being seasonally weak. This was broadly driven by strong sustenance sales, which highlights the underlying demand strength,” analysts at MOFSL said.
 
Balance sheet of the sector remains healthy, with net debt (ex-Lotus Developers) declining by ₹1,400 crore quarter-on-quarter (QoQ) (down by 76 per cent after FY17). Companies have broadly maintained their FY27 guidance, and analysts at MOFSL expect DLF, Prestige Estates Projects, Oberoi Realty, Brigade Enterprises and Lodha Developers to outperform peers in H2FY27. Valuations are comfortable, with larger developers trading closer to net asset value (NAV) and most small-medium companies trading at 20-65 per cent discount to the residential NAV, the brokerage firm said.
 
Meanwhile, analysts at Axis Securities remain constructive on the Real Estate sector, with H2FY27 expected to benefit from an expanded project launch pipeline and continued geographical diversification. The strong response to Oberoi Realty's first NCR project, alongside healthy demand across Prestige's Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Mumbai and Chennai markets, reinforces the resilience of premium housing demand. 
 
Developers continue to maintain disciplined balance sheets while actively pursuing land acquisitions, joint development agreements and new project opportunities. Rising disposable incomes, urbanisation, and premiumisation are expected to sustain housing demand. The brokerage firm believes the next phase of sector growth will be driven primarily by new launches, project execution and geographical expansion rather than aggressive price appreciation.
 
Analysts at PL Capital maintain a constructive stance on developers with strong launch pipelines, balance sheet discipline, and execution track record. Preference remains for players with Bengaluru/Mumbai exposure, premium positioning, and near-term launch visibility, which are best placed to sustain pre-sales growth into FY27E. Disclaimer: Views and outlook in this report belong to the brokerages and analysts cited. They do not reflect the views of Business Standard. Readers are advised to exercise discretion.

data.title: India ranks third in Asia power index; Modi second-most effective leader
data.description:
India has consolidated its position as the third-most powerful country and a "major powerhouse" in Asia, with Prime Minister Narendra Modi rated as the second most effective regional leader, according to the Lowly Institute's Asia Power Index 2026.

India's power score improved 0.5 to 40.5 points in the 2026 Index, taking its gap with China to the narrowest since 2018.

According to the Index, the US and China are "superpower in Asia for 2026" with a score 78.9 and 73.6, respectively out of 100.

India consolidated its major power status this year, growing more influential in Asia. Greater regional defence engagement and BrahMos missile sales to Southeast Asia strengthened its defence networks, while stable trade and investment ties made it one of the few countries whose economic relationships did not weaken.

 

"Its diplomatic influence held up as experts rated Prime Minister Narendra Modi the second-most effective regional leader after Xi Jinping, though India's low profile during the Gulf conflict weighed on views of his global leadership," the Asia Power Index 2026 said.

In 2026, India had the greatest gains in cultural influence (+2.3). It lost the most points in economic capability (-0.7). Elsewhere, it improved in defence networks (+2.1), future resources (+1.2) and military capability (+0.5). The scores for resilience, economic relationships and diplomatic influence were unchanged this year.

India's score in economic capability and cultural influence stood at 26.4 and 43.8, respectively, while its diplomatic influence score was at 70.3, as per the latest index.

The 2026 Lowy Institute Asia Power Index ranks 27 countries and territories across 131 indicators to measure who holds power in Asia.

According to the Index, the US-China power score has narrowed with just 5.3 points now separating the US (78.9) and China (73.6). This is the narrowest gap since the Index began in 2018. The military capability gap is also at its narrowest on record.

US Diplomatic Influence fell 6 points to 76.7, its largest drop on record and the fourth straight annual decline. Drivers include the Iran war, punitive tariffs and calls to scale back military exercises with South Korea.

"Despite upheaval, the regional balance of power remains markedly bipolar. The US and China still dominate, and neither a middle power bloc nor growing authoritarian alignment is displacing them," said Hunter Marston, Director of the Southeast Asia Program and Asia Power Index.

data.title: Brookfield agrees to acquire PGP Glass from Blackstone for $1.7 billion
data.description:
Brookfield Asset Management said on Monday ​it has agreed to ​acquire Indian glass packaging manufacturer ‌PGP Glass from Blackstone for $1.7 billion.

PGP Glass manufactures glass packaging for cosmetics, fragrances, spirits, food and pharmaceutical products.

"We welcome Brookfield and look forward to working with them to accelerate ‌our next phase of growth and value creation," PGP Glass CEO Vijay Shah said.

PGP Glass has 13 furnaces and a production capacity of ​more than 1,800 tonnes per day, according to ‌its website. It operates across markets ​including Brazil, ‌India, and the UK.

New York-based Brookfield ‌Asset Management manages more than $1 trillion across asset ‌classes including ​infrastructure, renewable ​power, private equity, real estate and credit.

data.title: Jack Ma's Ant Group bets on Simplexity Robotics in China's humanoid race
data.description:
By Saritha Rai
 
Chinese physical AI startup Simplexity Robotics received $100 million in a funding round led by Jack Ma-backed Ant Group Co., betting that the startup can take on more established players in the country’s burgeoning robotics arena.
 
Simplexity’s pre-Series A funding round valued the company at $1.6 billion and was joined by existing investors including Tencent Holdings Ltd., HSG and Lanchi Ventures, chairman and co-founder Wang Kai told Bloomberg News. 
 
China’s humanoid robotics industry has taken an early lead over American rivals, accounting for 97% of the machines shipped in the first three quarters of 2026. A raft of new firms, fueled by a government policy push and a deep local supply chain, has flooded the market. The country’s economic planning body recently warned of a bubble risk in the sector.
 
 
Simplexity unveiled its second humanoid on Monday, touting the ability of the wheeled machine dubbed iX to prepare and serve beverages, fetch and deliver items and lead guided tours. Its early customers include Korean robotics startup Rlwrld Inc., Tsinghua University and forklift maker Hangcha Group Co., with which it has launched a warehouse sorting line, the startup said.
 
Ant Group’s latest outlay adds to a robotics portfolio that includes investments in Unitree, Astribot and Zeroth. 
 
Wang founded Simplexity last summer along with Jia Peng and Wang Jiajia. The trio are all former executives at electric-vehicle maker Li Auto. Within months the startup surpassed $1 billion in valuation, according to Wang.
 
“We bring the foundation models, the data sets, the supply chain and the customers all working together to advance commercial robots,” Wang said in an interview at the company’s campus in Mudu, a 2,500-year-old canal town on the western fringe of Taihu Lake in Suzhou. Nearby, developers tracked a robot stacking juices, soda and water on shelves, while others tweaked algorithms on screens.
 
The company designs both hardware and software, tailoring them to specific tasks and form types. It builds its entire software stack in-house, from native AI world models to the real-world data used to train them. 
 
With China’s labor costs rising, birthrates falling and its productive workforce shrinking, Wang believes robots could prove indispensable to the world’s second-largest economy. “Our robots target the work that people don’t want to do,” he said.
 
Simplexity’s first humanoid, an industrial model on a wheeled base, is deployed in manufacturing, logistics sorting, retail and pharmaceutical packaging. The company has trained it to run CNC machines, the precision tools that cut, drill and shape metal, wood and plastic, and it seeks to address an acute shortage of operators. 
 
China has 3 million such machines and the average age of an operator is 45, according to Wang. With an average salary of about $20,000 a year, few young Chinese workers want the job, he said. “It’s a noisy, tough environment, you inhale a lot of dust,” he said. “We want the robots to conquer that type of work.”
 
The startup runs what it calls the world’s first intelligent CNC robot production line for Leaderdrive, one of its main customers and a key supplier to US robot makers Tesla Inc. and Figure AI Inc. Robots run round-the-clock production of precision motion-control components. Other customers include precision-parts maker Suzhou Dongshan Precision Manufacturing Co. as well as Hangcha.
 
Simplexity is also building China’s first modular humanoid arm with independently configurable joint modules that allow the arms to be disassembled and reconfigured with different lengths to suit specific tasks.
 
While the Chinese market is ferociously competitive, Wang calls that an advantage. “If we can sell and survive here, we can sell at bigger margins anywhere in the world,” he said.
 
If OpenAI built the killer chatbot and Anthropic PBC the best coding agent, Wang said his startup wants to build the breakout app of embodied AI, an ambition he shares with many of his Chinese peers. “We can have many knights, but there’s only one Arthur,” he said, likening the company’s ambitions to the legendary medieval British figure.
